scope: Theorem A (Regular-lifespan kinetic limit) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Φ satisfy Assumption 2.1, and let β > 0. Let f0 ≥ 0 be a C1 probability density on R3 × R3 such that ∥f0∥Bol,2β + ∥∇xf0∥Bol,2β < ∞. (1.3) Fix 0 < T < ∞ for which the equation (∂t + v · ∇x)f = QΦ(f, f), f|t=0 = f0, (1.4) has a nonnegative classical probability-density solution satisfying sup 0≤t≤T sup x,v e2β|v|2 f(t, x, v) < ∞. (1.5) Start the exact Newtonian process from the grand-canonical law (2.7). For its scaled factorial densities Fε s , defined in (2.8), every fixed integer s ≥ 1 satisfies lim ε↓0 sup 0≤t≤T ⃦ ⃦Fε s (t) − f(t)⊗s ⃦ ⃦ L1((R3×R3)s) = 0. (1.6)
